newsitem.title: UK: Higher Chicago futures subdue European veg oils.
newsitem.headline: Higher Chicago futures subdue European veg oils.

text.p: Higher Chicago soy futures on Thursday afternoon subdued trading on the European vegetable oil market.
The U.S. market had been expected to open lower after the USDA increased its estimate of the soybean carry-over figure and left Brazilian output unchanged.
However, Commission house buying at the Chicago opening forced soybeans higher in fast trading and bought business in Europe to a halt.
Earlier a strong dollar against European currencies and higher Chicago futures overnight on weather concerns supported prices.
But by the close sellers had backed off slightly and Dutch soy oil finished 1.75 to 0.50 guilders up while rape oil was 0.75 to 1.50 guilders higher in tradeless markets.
Coconut oil closed unchanged to $2.50 up while palmkernel oil was $7.50 higher.
As expected little interest was seen owing to the local holiday in the Philippines.

Palm oil prices were mixed but movements were minimal with the market expected to remain quiet ahead of the Wong report due for release on Friday and the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority official output, stocks and export data expected on Monday.
Malaysian plantation houses estimated an increase in May palm oil output at between four and 10 percent on Thursday.
At the close crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged to $2.50 down after Jun traded at $542.50 and $545, Aug/Sep at $532.50 and Oct/Dec at $530 a tonne cif.
RBD palm oil offers were $2.50 up in a tradeless market while olein was $2.50 down to unchanged with no further business reported.
